cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: strength – The capacity of an individual or group to withstand pressure or force.

p.em: Example: Real power comes from collective strength rather than top-down authority.

cosy-blockquote.p: voice – The sound produced in speaking or singing, or the right to express an opinion.

p.em: Example: Using your voice to lift others creates genuine grassroots change.

cosy-blockquote.p: truth – The real facts about something, unvarnished by corporate spin.

p.em: Example: Standing firm in your truth commands respect that money cannot buy.

cosy-blockquote.p: power – The ability or capacity to do something or act in a particular way.

p.em: Example: Real power belongs to the people when they unite for a common purpose.

cosy-blockquote.p: freedom – The state of being free or at liberty from oppressive restriction.

p.em: Example: Reclaiming your personal freedom starts with refusing to be manipulated.

cosy-blockquote.p: town – An urban area with a fixed boundary, symbolizing local community.

p.em: Example: Change begins right in your own town through community organizing.

cosy-blockquote.p: force – Strength or energy as an attribute of physical action or movement.

p.em: Example: A united community is an unstoppable force for positive reform.

cosy-blockquote.p: unity – The state of being united or joined as a whole.

p.em: Example: Building unity across differences turns isolated voices into a choir.

cosy-blockquote.p: stand – Maintain an upright position, or take a determined position on an issue.

p.em: Example: When you take a firm stand, you inspire others to do the same.

cosy-blockquote.p: noise – A sound, especially one that is loud or unpleasant; public outcry.

p.em: Example: Making enough noise forces those in authority to pay attention.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: They possess a real power of → Correct: They possess real power in leadership ((Omit 'a' before abstract noun 'power' when speaking generally.))
Incorrect: It is unity what gives us strength → Correct: It is unity that gives us strength ((Use 'that' or 'which' in cleft sentences: 'It is [noun] that [verb]'.))
Incorrect: They took a stand on front of → Correct: They took a stand in front of the building ((Use the correct fixed prepositional phrase 'in front of'.))
